full_judgment:
2. The short facts of the case are that the decree holder respondent instituted Title Suit No. 55 of 1986 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka, against the judgment-debtor petitioner as defendants for realization of Tie 84,50,000/-. Subsequently the suit was renumbered as Title Suit No. 18 of 1997. After several dates the suit was fixed for hearing on 31.8.1999 but since the defendant remained absent and took no step in the matter the suit was decreed exparte against the defendant judgment-debtor for an amount of Tk. 84,50,000/-. The decree was drawn up and signed on 15.9.1999. Thereafter the decree holder respondent that is the plaintiff in the said suit started Execution Case No. 2 of 1999 on 29.11.1999. On that date the execution case was registered and show cause notice was issued upon the defendant fixing 30.1.2000 for taking steps. On 30.1.2000 an order was passed to the effect that notice was returned after service. The decree holder appeared and the defendants No. 1 and 4 filed power and prayed for time to file written objection which the prayers was allowed and 23.2.2000 was fixed for filing objection. 

 3. The order dated 29.11.1999 for issuance of service of notice upon the judgment-debtors was challenged before the High Court Division and Rule was issued. It was submitted before the High Court Division that the Execution Case was filed under Order 21, Rule 11 of he Code of Civil Procedure and the court was required to proceed with the case and there was no provision for issuing notice upon the judgment-debtors if the execution case had been filed within two years from the date of decree. Order 21, Rule 22 of the Code of Civil Procedure provides that if the execution case is filed after two years from the date of decree then the show cause notice ought to be issued upon the judgment-debtor. In the instant case the decree was drawn up and signed on 15.9.1999 and the execution case was tiled on 29.11.1999. Since the execution case was filed within three months from the date of passing the decree issuance of notices upon the judgment-debtor was absolutely illegal and without jurisdiction. It was further submitted before the High Court Division the suit was filed in the year 1986 and the decree obtained in the year 1999 and in order to cause delay in the execution proceeding and also to obstruct the decree-holders from getting the benefit of the decree the judgment-debtors were taking time to file written objection though in law there was no provision for filing objection. The High Court Division after bearing both the parties accepted the submission made by the decree-holders and held that the court below acted in a manner which was not provided in law and that the process of execution of the decree would be delayed to the prejudice of the decree-holders, As such the High Court Division found that the orders Passed on 29.11.1999 as well as 30.1.2000 by the Executing Court in Execution Case No. 2 of 1999 could not be sustained in law. The executing court in passing on above mentioned orders had committed an error of law occasioning failure of justice and therefore made the Rule absolute with the direction to proceed with the execution ease in accordance with law expeditiously.
